subject: Last-mile capacity top-up and early payment discount
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@clearcart.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Short-notice capacity lift for holiday campaign

Hey Logan,

We're putting a last-mile push for a promotional window that starts tomorrow night and runs through Monday morning. Traffic spike estimates attached (traffic_forecast_nov26.csv) — looks like we need about a 3x uplift in sustained throughput for ~72 hours to avoid errors on checkout flows.

Two quick asks: can Redwood do a short-notice temporary top-up for that window? If so, what's the commercial — both price and how you handle metering/overrun true-ups? Also, if we prepay the uplift fee or commit a small short-term addendum now, can we get any discount? We're ready to sign a PO today if you can move fast.

Appreciate a rapid turnaround — our campaign can’t afford throttling.

Thanks,
Jared Cole
Head of Ops, ClearCart Retail Inc.
finance@clearcart.com
(attachment: traffic_forecast_nov26.csv)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-26T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Short-notice capacity lift for holiday campaign

Jared — thanks for the heads up and the forecast. We can support a short-notice uplift; I ran a quick check with runtime and I have two practical paths:

1) Temporary top-up (72 hours): one-time uplift fee + standard per-token usage during the window. Fast to approve and we can activate within 2 hours of signed PO.

2) Short committed uplift (7–30 day min): lower per-token during the uplift but requires a short addendum/commit.

For immediate purposes, option (1) is the fastest. I attached a preliminary quote (capacity_topup_quote_v3.pdf) with pricing bands and an early-payment concession option. If you can prepay the uplift fee (we can accept wired payment within 7 days), we can apply a discount to the one-time uplift fee.

Can you confirm which option you prefer and share the PO contact? I’ll loop in finance to lock timing.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: capacity_topup_quote_v3.pdf)

Attached my draft quote. Need quick guidance on concession bounds and billing path:
- Can we offer a time-limited early-pay discount?
- How do we do metering/true-up for the uplift window without dragging PO timelines?

I’d prefer a clean transient top-up with a one-time uplift fee and a small % off if they pay within 7 days. If we offer a deeper discount, we should require a short commitment or increased PO value.

We need a pricing decision within the hour to get docs ready for their legal/procurement.

—Logan

Logan — agree with the transient-top-up approach for speed. My recommended structure:

- Option A (fastest): 72-hour transient top-up, one-time uplift fee = $12,500 + normal usage (metered). If ClearCart prepays uplift fee within 7 days, give 10% off the uplift fee (i.e., $11,250). No change to per-token rate.
- Option B (better price if they want cheaper per-token): 14-day minimum short-commit uplift, reduced per-token unit cost (-12%) but requires signed addendum and higher PO value.

Given the timing, offer Option A with the 10% early-pay concession. If legal asks for more, we can escalate.

Also note: we should require a PO that references deal CC-8721 and include the final invoice schedule. I’ll stand by to approve the concession.

—Ben

All — finance OK on the 10% early-pay discount for the uplift fee but a couple constraints:

1) Payment terms for the discounted uplift must be met (wired payment cleared within 7 days) or discount is void.
2) PO must reference the unique invoice id we issue and be received before activation. We can accept a scanned PO (PDF) via email with a follow-up e-signature.
3) We will prorate the monthly invoice to reflect normal usage vs uplift window and include line items that clearly separate uplift fee from metered usage.

Attached a PO stub to send the customer (ClearCart_PO_8327_stub.pdf) — it includes the required invoice reference fields. If you'd like, I can issue the invoice once I get the PO copy and confirmation of payment method.

—Laura
